parts.description: A brushed stainless-steel teapot with a tapered cylindrical body, curved spout, domed lid, and black insulated handle. The metal surfaces have a satin silver finish with small vent holes in the lid.
parts.reasoning: No exact product data is visible, so values are estimated for an empty stainless-steel teapot of roughly 0.16-0.18 m body diameter, 0.16-0.20 m height, and 0.28-0.32 m total length including spout and handle. A thin-wall stainless teapot of this size typically weighs about 0.6-0.9 kg empty; 0.75 kg is a practical rigid-body mass. The dominant structural/contact material is brushed stainless steel, so the material density is set to approximately 7850 kg/m^3. Because the teapot is hollow, the mass should preferably be authored explicitly rather than computed from a coarse convex hull density; if automatic mass-from-collider is used with simplified filled convex volumes, an effective density near 150-250 kg/m^3 may be needed to recover the same total mass. The main bottom/body contacts are stainless steel, giving moderate dry friction: about 0.45 static and 0.35 dynamic. Restitution is set to 0.50, the low end for steel, because the hollow sheet-metal body, lid, and polymer handle dissipate impact energy more than a solid steel part. The geometry is not well represented by a single convex hull because of the curved spout, handle loop, lid knob, and tapered body; a compound convex decomposition is recommended, using separate convex pieces for the body, lid/knob, spout segments, and handle brackets/grip. Dynamic triangle mesh collision should be avoided for performance and robustness. Small positive rest/contact offsets are chosen to stabilize contact without visibly inflating the object; CCD is recommended because the spout and lid lip are relatively thin and could tunnel during drops or fast manipulation. Sleep and velocity limits are selected for a tabletop-sized metal object to reduce jitter and avoid excessive depenetration impulses.
